MX.name: Mexico
MX.summary: Querétaro holds most of Mexico's data-centre capacity and is also one of the states with the highest water stress, per Expansión (27 May 2026). Grid connection is the binding constraint: CFE substation energisations for data-centre loads are reported in January 2026, and the state governor publicly disputed a former regulator's claim of an energy deficit in September 2026. The state has said it will publish water-use data for data centres from 2027, after a 2026 pilot, though that is secondary reporting.
MX._context_note: Context fact from Expansión 2026-05-27 (verbatim in records). Not yet shaped to ContextFact: needs translation object.

ES.name: Spain
ES.summary: Aragón is the centre of Spain's data-centre build-out. AWS campuses are approved through regional PIGA plans and an environmental authorisation (Inaga, July 2026) that sets a city water cap, and local campaigns and a court challenge contest the water and energy impacts. National grid-access rules for large loads were tightened by RDL 7/2026 (unverified against BOE).

regulators.name: Comisión Nacional de los Mercados y la Competencia

BE.name: Belgium
BE.summary: Wallonia hosts Google's St. Ghislain campus, the largest data-centre site in the country, and Google announced a two-year EUR 5 billion expansion there in October 2025. Grid capacity is allocated by Elia, and the energy regulator CREG tightened its code of conduct in January 2026 so that unbuilt projects lose reserved capacity (secondary reporting, not yet verified against CREG text).
